about: Papers opened in LH035's bounded literature check (eight searches, at most twelve papers), 2 November 2026. Each was read at least to its method and limits unless marked failed. PDFs the fetch tool could not parse were saved by the tool and their text extracted with pdftotext (poppler); the extracted text was read with grep and sed, and the passages used are quoted below.

papers.cite: Durumeric, Clark, Cody, Cubit, Ellison, Izhikevich, Mirian. Censys: A Map of Internet Hosts and Services. ACM SIGCOMM 2025.
papers.method: Coverage against a random 0.1% sub-sample of IPv4 services across all 65K ports scanned with ZMap for one week from 20 August 2024 (4.1 million services), and against Shodan, Fofa, ZoomEye and Netlas by querying 10K random addresses.
papers.findings: "Censys sees 98% of IPv4-based services on the top 10 ports, 97% of the top 100 ports, and 62% of services across all 65K ports"; daily BigQuery snapshots, after three months one weekday snapshot a week kept; 1,221 researchers given access 2018 to 2024.
papers.limits: Written by Censys's own staff. "we do not conduct comprehensive IPv6 scans" and IPv6 is not evaluated; "no ground truth dataset of Internet services exists"; "We restrict access to data that is ripe for abuse"; "intelligent 65K port scanning remains an unsolved problem"; other engines "do not provide access to raw data", so comparison is indirect.

papers.cite: Bennett, Abdou, van Oorschot. Empirical Scanning Analysis of Censys and Shodan. NDSS MADWeb workshop 2021.
papers.method: Virtual machines in five locations (San Jose, Tokyo, Montreal, Paris, Sao Paulo) on AWS ran four services and recorded scans and banner grabs; planted tokens measured freshness.
papers.findings: "both engines made all captured tokens visible within 24 hours"; 65% within about 15 hours; Shodan 20% within 5 hours.
papers.limits: Described by its authors as an in-progress snapshot; "Censys/Shodan maybe scanning Amazon's AWS VMs different from non-Amazon devices"; TCP only.

papers.cite: Le Pochat, Van Goethem, Tajalizadehkhoob, Korczynski, Joosen. Tranco: A Research-Oriented Top Sites Ranking Hardened Against Manipulation. NDSS 2019.
papers.how_read: HTML, first 100,000 of 107,266 characters through the fetch tool
papers.method: Alexa, Umbrella, Majestic and Quantcast lists from 1 January to 30 November 2018; similarity, stability, representativeness, responsiveness, benignness; manipulation experiments; survey of 133 papers.
papers.findings: The four lists held about 2.82 million sites and agreed on about 70,000; Umbrella changed about 10% a day; all four were manipulated.
papers.limits: Tranco inherits its sources' biases and they "remain susceptible to manipulation" if all are manipulated; findings tied to provider behaviour in 2018.

papers.cite: Certificate Perspectives (IMC 2016), as titled in the search result; not read.
papers.limits: The search summary's figure (90.5% of browser-trusted certificates in CT logs) was not read in the paper and is not used.

papers.cite: Sermpezis, Prehn, Kostoglou, Flores, Vakali, Aben. Bias in Internet Measurement Platforms. arXiv 2307.09958 (v2, July 2023).
papers.search: P5 result 1 (opened as the abstract page and the HTML version)
papers.method: Bias as the distance between the distribution of more than 100,000 ASes and of the ASes hosting vantage points, over 22 characteristics; Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests and a bounded KL divergence score 0 to 1.
papers.findings: Average bias Atlas 0.06, RIS 0.16, RouteViews 0.15, combined collectors 0.14, a random sample 0.00 to 0.01; "RIPE RIS is heavily biased towards larger networks and IXPs"; Atlas default probe selection about twice as biased as random.
papers.limits: AS level only; "only 25% of ASNs have records in PeeringDB"; not every dimension matters to every study; effects on results not studied.

papers.cite: Alfroy, Holterbach, Krenc, Claffy, Pelsser. Measuring Internet Routing from the Most Valuable Points. arXiv 2405.13172 (v1, May 2024).
papers.how_read: HTML, first 100,000 of 106,308 characters through the fetch tool
papers.method: Scores RIS and RouteViews vantage points by redundancy using about 7,500 new-link events and 15 topological features; simulation and comparison with a private collector.
papers.findings: "A tiny fraction (1.3%) of the 74k ASes" host a vantage point, 8.4% of transit ASes; RIS 1,526 and RouteViews 1,071 vantage points in May 2023; bgp.tools saw 192k AS links no RIS or RouteViews point saw, and they saw 401k it missed.
papers.limits: Simulated topology differs from the real one; "cannot know how much additional topology we might observe from VPs that do not peer with the public collection systems"; approximate ground truth for hijacks.

papers.cite: Sommese, van Rijswijk-Deij, Jonker. This Is a Local Domain: On Amassing Country-Code Top-Level Domains from Public Data. arXiv 2309.01441 (preprint, September 2023).
papers.search: P3 result 2 (opened as the abstract page and the HTML version)
papers.method: Registered domains under ccTLDs from 38 CT logs (certificates valid from 2017) and 58 Common Crawl snapshots (June 2017 to June 2023), compared yearly on 1 June 2018 to 2023 with OpenINTEL zone data for 19 ccTLDs.
papers.findings: In 2023 the public sources covered 43% (.us) to 80% (.ee) of zones, weighted 59%; CT 52%, Common Crawl 31%, Common Crawl alone 7%; 37% in 2018.
papers.limits: 19 of over 300 ccTLDs, "may be somewhat biased towards specific regions"; CT gives no reliable publication time; only CT and Common Crawl examined.

papers.cite: Aqeel, Chandrasekaran, Feldmann, Maggs. On Landing and Internal Web Pages: The Strange Case of Jekyll and Hyde in Web Performance Measurement. ACM IMC 2020.
papers.method: Landing and internal pages of 1,000 sites compared; 119 web-performance papers from 2015 to 2019 reviewed; Hispar list built.
papers.findings: Internal pages "differ substantially" from landing pages; 41 papers need no revision, 48 minor and 30 major, so "nearly two-thirds" need revision to apply to internal pages.
papers.limits: "sample bias of selecting the top roughly 2000 web sites"; does not measure pages "behind a user log-in".

papers.cite: Degen, Kempen, claffy, Mok, Holz, van Rijswijk-Deij, Sommese, Jonker. Through a Smaller Lens: Revisiting Opportunistic Analysis using Network Telescopes. 2026 (hosted in CAIDA's catalogue; venue not recorded).
papers.method: Traffic to three telescopes (UCSD-NT 10.9 million monitored addresses, MERIT-NT 476 thousand, SURF-NT 66.3 thousand) in April 2025, replicating a study of ten years before.
papers.findings: "smaller telescopes offer higher visibility per monitored address"; "37.0% of them targeting a /16 block in each of the three telescopes within an hour"; "larger telescopes detect many attacks missed by smaller ones".
papers.limits: Shorter period and smaller telescopes than the original study; UCSD-NT captures unavailable 2025-04-11 18:00 to 23:59; seven random one-hour samples for some analyses.

papers.cite: Parla. Efficacy of EPSS in High Severity CVEs found in CISA KEV. arXiv 2411.02618 (v1, November 2024), single author, independent.
papers.method: 90 KEV entries with CVSS 9.0 or more added 15 March 2023 to 1 July 2024; EPSS score histories against disclosure, listing and first exploitation dates.
papers.findings: 42 of 57 KEV entries from 2023 or later had consistently low EPSS before listing; more than two thirds of 250 KEV entries in the period were below 36% just before listing.
papers.limits: Small purposive sample; EPSS features and data not public; KEV "is also a subset of all exploited CVEs"; untested assumptions.

papers.cite: Gustafsson, Overier, Arlitt, Carlsson. A First Look at the CT Landscape: Certificate Transparency Logs in Practice. PAM 2017.
papers.method: A monitor over the public logs submitted to Chrome to December 2015 (three Google, seven CA-operated) and NORDUnet's log, beside 232 million HTTPS sessions on a university network.
papers.findings: "for almost all domains observed in the university traces, there is at least one log with a valid DV certificate (despite such logging being voluntary for all CAs except Symantec)".
papers.limits: Data end in 2015, before CT was required by browsers; one campus's traffic.
